ThingDef.label: Hunter drone auto-deployment platform
ThingDef.description:
The Hunter is the most common light combat drone in corporate systems, widely used for frontier patrols, facility security, and asset protection. It carries two light machine guns, using strong mobility and persistent tracking to suppress ground infantry, and is especially effective at chasing hostile personnel who leave the battle line or attempt to flank. Its lightweight frame, however, can barely withstand dedicated anti-air fire.

When deployed independently, a Hunter autonomously searches for nearby targets. Multiple units can also enable harassment mode to tie down different enemies. Once a drone command console is installed, an operator can coordinate the whole group and order them to rapidly redeploy to a designated area.

Corporate security manuals claim that Hunters significantly reduce patrol workload.
An old guard agreed: "We used to have to chase people ourselves."
He looked up as three drones flew past, then added, "Now we only have to explain why they chased the wrong people."

ThingDef.label: Tinker Drone dock
ThingDef.description: A compact support platform that launches a Tinker Drone to repair nearby turrets and replenish their ammunition reserves. Requires both low-altitude autonomous navigation and autonomous maintenance doctrine before construction.

ThingDef.label: drone command console
ThingDef.description: A centralized tactical console for assigning patrol zones to networked drones. It marks a radius-5 command area and orders active Hunter combat drones to move there, patrol the zone, and prioritize threats within it.

ThingDef.label: JUDGMENT DAY support uplink
ThingDef.description: A tactical support uplink for calling the JUDGMENT DAY super-heavy aerial weapons platform. Hack the control terminal to authorize one platform call. The system re-locks after use and can be hacked again after three days.

li.notHackedInspectString: Hack to authorize one JUDGMENT DAY call.

ThingDef.label: HAD-09 Ghoul drone bomber bay
ThingDef.description: The HAD-09 "Ghoul" is a high-altitude unmanned bomber designed for deep strikes and critical-target destruction. Unlike the Hunter, which is built for sustained patrol and close support, the Ghoul does not linger over the battlefield. After target identification, it rapidly enters an attack course, launching micro-missiles at multiple targets inside the selected area or dropping a 500kg-class aerial bomb to devastate fire positions and assembly zones.\n\nAfter completing its mission, it must return to remote airspace for resupply, maintenance, and route reprogramming, so it cannot be called continuously. Against guerrilla forces that lack stable air defense and rely on concealed strongholds, however, the Ghoul usually only needs to appear once to cast the entire area into long-term panic.

ThingDef.label: mechanoid manta
ThingDef.description: A disposable hostile mechanoid flyer that tracks and attacks colonists and turrets, flying over defensive lines and walls.

ThingDef.label: mechanoid bombard manta
ThingDef.description: A heavy hostile mechanoid flyer that locks a ground position before dropping a high explosive bomb. Mobile targets can evade the strike if they move before the lock completes.

ThingDef.label: Tinker Drone
ThingDef.description: A compact autonomous engineering drone that patrols from its dock to repair damaged turrets, replenish turret ammunition, and return to its station when idle.

ThingDef.label: 实验型采矿无人机
ThingDef.description: 一架用于验证深层矿脉自动采掘流程的实验无人机。它会飞向最近已扫描出的深层矿物并持续采掘，暂未安装内置电量和充电逻辑。
